Council Meeting Minutes for
City of Cabot, Arkansas
508 N. Lincoln
Cabot, AR 72023
December 16, 2024
6:30 pm.

This event was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed
here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmwHZpyOfNw.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 6:30
pm. Council Member Steven Redd led the prayer, and Council Member James Reid led
the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Corey Spangler, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Ed Long,
and Ron Waymack. Matt Webber was absent. Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben
Hooper, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom also attended.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Hillenburg, seconded by Mr. Spangler, motioned to approve the December 2
council meeting minutes. The motion passed with a vote of 6-0-1. Mr. Reid
Abstained from voting.

Mr. Reid, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned only to read the legislation by title
only. The motion passed unanimously.

City Council
OLD BUSINESS: None

NEW BUSINESS: RESOLUTION NO. 60 OF 2024 -— A RESOLUTION
ESTABLISHING THE CITY COUNCIL 2025 MEETING CALENDAR; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES was read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.
Mr. Long, seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned to adopt. The motion passed
unanimously.

RESOLUTION NO. 61 OF 2024 — A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR
AND CITY CLERK/TREASURER TO ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH RED
RIVER DODGE FOR THE PURCHASE OF A VEHICLE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
was read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Hillenburg,
seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned to adopt. The motion passed unanimously.

SECTION 4.7 SPECIAL PERMIT USES

4.7.1 What is a Special Permit Use?

A Special Permit Use is a use that conforms to the intent of the comprehensive plan for a specific
area and is generally allowable but not by right at any location. The use may represent potential
problems with respect to its impact on neighboring property or to the city as a whole, or it may
dominate the surrounding area by its size or intensity. For these reasons, special permit uses
require a careful review of their location, design, configuration, and spatial impact to determine the
desirability of allowing them on a particular site.

The Special Permit Use process must not allow an applicant to secure a use variance or as a
means to circumvent the intent of the comprehensive plan or zoning code. Building configurations,
footprints, and outlines should be compatible with other uses permitted for a district. Whether a
proposed use is appropriate in a particular location depends upon a careful evaluation of the
impacts to the neighborhood and the city by the Planning Commission and a weighing of conditions
and methods proposed by the commission or by the applicant to ameliorate those impacts.

4.7.2 Uses

Uses which are listed in various districts as "special permit uses" may be located only in the district
or districts so designated and in accordance with the procedure described herein in Section 4.7.5.

4.7.3 Standards

The Planning Commission may approve, deny, defer, or modify a special permit use request based
on findings of fact with regard to the standards set forth below. The appropriateness of these

Conditions

The Planning Commission may impose conditions and restrictions upon the premises benefited by

intent of this Code. The Planning Commission shall not permit any use in a zone as a special
permit use that is not permitted under the zoning cade.

Conditions imposed as part of the special permit use may be of two types. Threshold Conditions
are those that must be met by all proposed developments before an application for a special permit
use will be forwarded to the Planning Commission. Implicit Conditions are those that the Planning

Procedure for Authorizing

a. Application; Application for a special permit use shall be made by the property owner or

authorized agent for the owner. The application shall be submitted to the Public Works Office
which will process all applicable surveys, site plans and other supporting information pertinent
to this review process and make recommendations to the planning commission.

Notice of the Special Permit Use application shall be published at least one time, not less than fifteen
(15) days prior to the date of the public hearing, in a newspaper of general circulation. The
applicant shall give notice of such hearing by posting a suitable and pertinent sign, provided by

the city, onthe property involved not less than fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing.

Development plan requirements: The development plan requirements for a special permit use
application shall include a graphic representation of what is proposed and a general statement
as to the intent of the use. The graphic representation shall include the following:

i. The location, size and use of buildings, signs, land and improvements
ii. The location, size and arrangement of parking space, loading space,

iii. driveways and street access

iv. The existing topography with proposed grading and drainage plans

v. Proposed screening and landscaping

vi. The use of adjoining property

vii. Scale, north arrow and vicinity map

viii. Any additional information needed by the staff because of conditions peculiar to the development.
Development plan review: The Public Works staff shall review the proposed special permit

use and report to the commission on its relation to and probable effect on the surrounding

area as well asits compliance with the requirements of this Code and shall make
recommendations to the Planning Commission.

Planning Commission Action: The Planning Commission shall review special permit use
applications at its regularly scheduled monthly meeting, at which time interested persons may
appear and offer information in support of, or against the proposed special permit use. The
Planning Commission shall then make one of the following determinations: approve the special
permit use as requested; approve the special permit use with modifications; defer the special
permit use; or deny the special permit use.

The Planning Commission may impose conditions and restrictions upon the premises benefited
by a special permit use as may be necessary to reduce or minimize the injurious effects of the
special permit use, ensure compatibility with the surrounding property and carry out the general
intent of the comprehensive plan, appropriate neighborhood plans and this code.

operative. The violation of any condition so imposed shall constitute grounds for revocation of
the special permit use. Such conditions may include time limits for exercise of such
authorization and must commence within a reasonable time.

The Board of Adjustment is not authorized to grant a variance from conditions imposed by the
commission in connection with a special permit use. However, the Board of Adjustment may
grant variances as provided by the Zoning Code.

Amendments or major changes to a special permit use authorization must follow the same
process as the original special permit use; however, the Commission may delegate to the staff
authority to approve minor modifications to the conditions approved, including modifications to
an approved development plan. No building permit shall be issued except in conformance with
the provisions of this section.

A Special Permit Use is a part of the Zoning Code and shall run with the land upon which the
use is located.

4.7.6 Fees
Before any action shall be taken as provided in this section, the petitioner shall deposit with the City
an application fee as established or may hereafter be adopted by resolution of the City Council.
Under no condition shall said sum or any part thereof be refunded for failure of said permit to be
approved by the Planning Commission.

4.7.7 Special Permit Uses and Rezoning
Special permit use applications and rezoning applications for the same lot, parcel, or development
site may be processed by the city concurrently. However, the special permit use cannot be in
operation until the city council has adopted an ordinance rezoning the property to an appropriate
zone that would allow the special permit use, and the adopting ordinance has taken effect.

ORDINANCE NO. 1 OF 2025

AN ORDINANCE CONCERNING CABOT CITY COUNCIL PROCEDURE FOR THE
ABANDONMENT OF RIGHTS-OF-WAY; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council herein recognizes and reaffirms that it has sole
legal authority over the abandonment and any other permanent closure (jointly referred to herein
as abandonment) of city streets, public alleyways, and other public rights-of-way; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council finds that it is appropriate to consider the effect on
surrounding businesses that a right-of-way closure may have, especially in regards to the
Americans with Disabilities Act and other related considerations; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council desires to set forth and mandate that the above be
taken into consideration prior to a public right-of-way being abandoned; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council herein acknowledges that it has sole legal
authority to abandon or otherwise permanently close a city street, public alleyway, and other
public rights-of-way. Said authority may only be exercised through majority vote of the Cabot
City Council.

SECTION 2: Prior to abandoning or otherwise permanently closing a right-of-way, the
Cabot City Council shall consider any effect on surrounding businesses said closure may have,
especially any effect in regards to the Americans with Disabilities Act and other related
considerations.

SECTION 3: This legislation is in regards to right-of-way abandonments and other
permanent closures. Nothing herein effects the City’s authority to temporarily close city streets,
public alleyways, and other public rights-of-way as permitted by law.

SECTION 4: If any provision of this Ordinance is found to be invalid by the decision

of any court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining sections,

City Council Meeting Organizational Structure

1. Work Session Meetings

Work Session meetings shall customarily be held on the first Monday of every month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed.
These Work Session meetings are utilized to allow council members and each standing committee
to discuss details of proposed legislation with City staff in a more informal setting. The Work
Session shall be called to order by the Mayor who will then recognize the chair of each committee
in turn to discuss the items on the agenda relevant to that committee. Each committee chair shall
preside over the discussion of agenda items relevant to his or her committee and may conduct
votes amongst his committee members to forward any piece of proposed legislation on to a regular
council meeting or for any other appropriate purpose. No readings or votes for final passage of
legislation shall be conducted during Work Session meetings.

At the conclusion of each Work Session meeting, a Regular Session Council meeting shall
be held. At this meeting any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action
may be taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. This meeting need not be conducted
if there are no items on its agenda for consideration.

2. Regular Session Meeting

Regular Session meetings shall customarily be held on the third Monday of each month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed. At
these meetings any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action may be
taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. Pursuant to state law, these meetings shall
be presided over by the Mayor, with each council member having an opportunity to discuss any
item, make any appropriate motion, and vote when appropriate.

Only items on the agenda may be discussed, read, or voted on, unless the agenda is
amended to add that particular item by 2/3 vote of all elected council members. An item not on
the agenda may be discussed, though not voted on, during the community input section of the
meeting.

Pursuant to state law, any motion to suspend the rules, waive readings, approve or attach
an emergency clause, or similar motion must be passed by 2/3 vote of all elected council members

4. Dates of Meetings

Specific dates of meetings shall be set out in other legislation adopted for that purpose.
Meeting dates may be changed as discussed in that legislation.

5. Agendas for Meetings

The agenda for the Work Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Any council member may request to have an item added to a Work Session meeting agenda. A
Work Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

The agenda for the Regular Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Items may be placed on this agenda by the Mayor, by majority vote of the Council, or by majority
vote of the appropriate committee at a Work Session meeting or other committee meeting. A
Regular Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

In order to be placed on an agenda, a legislative item must be sponsored by either a
council member or the Mayor. Ifa legislative item is forwarded to the Council from one of the
city’s independent commissions it must be sponsored by that independent commission.

Agendas are considered final once forwarded to council members and legislative items
may not be added after that point except upon 2/3 vote of all elected Council members. However,
an item may be added to the agenda after it was sent out but before the start of the meeting upon
joint agreement of the Mayor and the City Council President Pro Tempore.

6. President Pro Tempore

Ed Long, as longest serving member of the Cabot City Council, is hereby named City
Council President Pro Tempore.

7. Mayor and City Council Relationship

In exercising its management responsibilities, the City Council reserves its authority
to approve policy which represents broad statements of its intentions, approves plans and
programs, and delegates authority of administration to the Mayor, except those rights that
are by law conferred upon or reserved to the city council. Pursuant to state law, the City
Council delegates the authority to the Mayor to hire capable personnel within an approved
wage and salary policy, to plan and establish schedules and to train, supervise and terminate
employees. Per A.C.A. § 14-42-110, the City Council reserves the authority to review the
hiring or removal of a department head and may overturn the hiring or removal of a
department head by the Mayor upon two-thirds majority of all elected Council members.

8. Further Responsibilities of the Mayor

The Mayor has the principal responsibility for directing the operations of the city
government and for advising and assisting the City Council in its deliberations. In connection
with the latter responsibility, the City Council requests the Mayor to furnish it with whatever
data, information, and material it may need to properly carry out its functions in an informed
manner.

The Mayor also has the principal responsibility to ensure that the city's administrative
officers and department heads understand and obey all local, state, and federal laws
pertaining to the city's operations, and when a violation of any law is discovered, that
appropriate disclosure is made to the City Council and proper and adequate disciplinary
measures are taken against the responsible employee or employees.

9. Further Responsibilities of the Council

It is the responsibility of City Council members to be engaged and present at meetings in
representing the residents of Cabot. If any member of the City Council is absent for either three
consecutive meetings or four total meetings in a calendar year then a Resolution of Reprimand
shall be considered by the Council. Absences may be excused at a council member’s request and
by joint agreement of the Mayor and the President Pro Tempore of the City Council.

It is the further responsibility of council members to hold themselves to a high ethical and
moral standard in representing the residents of Cabot. Any member who fails to live up to these
standards or who brings embarrassment or disrepute to the City Council may also be subject to a
Resolution of Reprimand.

10. City Council and Mayor Cooperation

Efficient management of the city can exist only through mutual understanding and
complete cooperation between the City Council and the Mayor. The Mayor's performance
cannot be of the best unless he is given the latitude to exercise independent judgment in
executing policies of the City Council. The City Council acknowledges that obligation and
gives the Mayor the latitude of judgment and discretion, and expects faithful performance in
carrying out the policies of the City Council.

It shall be understood that administrative authority for the management of the city
rests with the Mayor. Members of the City Council should refrain, as individuals, from giving.
specific direction or instruction to city personnel pertaining to the discharge of assigned
duties, however, open communication between aldermen and city employees is encouraged.
and expected to guarantee sound decisions based upon the free flow of information.

11. Committees

There are five standing committees: Municipal Services; Budget and Personnel; Police and
Fire; Community Development; and Military Affairs. Additional committees may be added by
majority vote of the City Council. In January of each year that follows a regular city council
election, or reasonably soon thereafter, the City Council shall designate committee assignments
for its members through the passage of legislation. Once established by legislation, committee
assignments may be changed thereafter by majority vote of the City Council.

Each committee may have up to five members in total, which shall consist of up to four regular

members and a chair. Each separate committee shall vote to select its own chair, and the chair
may be changed thereafter by majority vote of that committee.

ARTICLE IV. FALSE ALARMS

Sec. 16-84. Purpose.

It shall be the purpose of this article to appropriately assess the costs incurred in response of those who
operate or own a private alarm system in or on a residential or business structure/property which continually or
repeatedly issues a false alarm.

(Code 1992, § 94.40; Ord. No. 37-2007, 9-17-2007)

Sec. 16-85. Violation.

It shall constitute a per se violation of the terms of this article when any subscriber has an alarm system
which provides a false alarm more than three times within any three-month period.

(Code 1992, § 94.41; Ord. No. 37-2007, 9-17-2007)

Sec. 16-86. Definition.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them
in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Alarm system means any mechanical or electrical device that is arranged, designed, or used to signal the
occurrence within the city of burglary, robbery, or other criminal offense, fire emergency, or medical emergency
requiring urgent attention which police, fire, or other municipal personnel are expected to respond. The term
“alarm system" shall include those through which public safety personnel and/or the police department are
notified directly or indirectly (by way of a third party person or party who monitors the alarm system and who
report such signal to the communications center, fire, or police department). The term “alarm system" shall also
include those systems designed to register an audio/visual signal so audible, visible, or in other ways perceptible
outside a protected building structure or facility as to where the signal is located which in turn is cause for a
reasonable person to notify emergency municipal officials of the signal. The term “alarm system" does not include
those designed and fixed to vehicles, nor does it include auxiliary devices installed by telephone companies to
protect telephone equipment or systems that may be damaged or disrupted by the use of an alarm system. Alarm
systems in separate structures are to be considered as separate systems even though the systems may be owned
by the same person or entity. A subscriber is any person, firm, corporation, partnership, or entity that purchases,
lease a contract for, or obtains an alarm system and/or monitoring service.

(Code 1992, § 94.42; Ord. No. 37-2007, 9-17-2007)

Sec. 16-87. False alarms.

A false alarm is an alarm signal eliciting a response by the police or fire department when a situation
requiring a response by the police or fire department does not in fact exist. A false alarm does not include an alarm
signal caused by violent conditions of nature or other extraordinary circumstances not reasonably subject to
control by the alarm business operator or alarm user. Alarms resulting from the following conditions will not be
considered false alarms: criminal activity or unauthorized entry; an alarm caused on the reasonable but mistaken
belief that a burglary, robbery, or other criminal offense, fire emergency, or medical emergency is in progress;

Refusal or failure of any subscriber to pay any fee assessment as provided herein shall result in issuance of a
violation of the terms of this article. Should a subscriber be issued a citation by the chief of police or his authorized
designee and be found guilty, plead guilty, or plead no contest of said violation in the city district court, the

shall direct that full payment of any outstanding fee assessments be paid to the city in full within a time designated
by the court. In the event the subscriber is a corporation, partnership, or other entity, the principal or employee
directly responsible for the operation of the enterprise at the location from which the false alarm initiates shall be
responsible for payment of any fine assessments levied in accordance with this article. A citation issued under this
Section may be issued to and served upon any party authorized to receive notice under Section 16-89

In addition to other consequences of nonpayment, unpaid fees assessed under Section 16-89 for commercial
false alarms shall be applied against the relevant business’s City of Cabot business license. Any fee assessed for
commercial false alarms under Section 16-89 and not paid within thirty days shall be added to the amount the
business is required to pay in order to renew their business license for the following year or for the next year said
business applies for a business license. In such cases, a business shall not receive a new or renewed business
license until all assessed fees under Section 16-89 are paid in full. A business may not operate in Cabot without a
business license and the City of Cabot is authorized to take any appropriate steps to ensure compliance with the

Sec. 16-91. Appeals

appeal said fee assessment. A Request for Appeal must be made in writing to the Chief of Police of the Cabot

the fee assessment in question. _ The written Request for Appeal must include the following: name, address,
email, and phone number of the appealing party; the reason that the appealing party believes the fee was
assessed in error; and any other relevant information that that appealing party wishes to have taken under
consideration. A Request for Appeal that is untimely or not in the proper form may be dismissed by the Chief
without a hearing.

The Chief shall conduct a hearing within 30 days of receiving a timely and proper Request for Appeal. The
Chief shall inform the appealing party of the date, time, and location of the hearing, and the appealing party shall
have the opportunity to appear and present any relevant information. The Chief shall determine, in light of any
information provided by the appealing party, if the fee at issue was reasonably assessed given the circumstances.
The Chief shall issue a decision to grant or deny the appeal within thirty days from the date of the hearing and shall
inform the appealing party of that decision in writing. The Chief shall also provide notice of his or her decision to

ORDINANCE NO. 1 OF 2025

AN ORDINANCE CONCERNING CABOT CITY COUNCIL PROCEDURE FOR THE
ABANDONMENT OF RIGHTS-OF-WAY; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council herein recognizes and reaffirms that it has sole
legal authority over the abandonment and any other permanent closure (jointly referred to herein
as abandonment) of city streets, public alleyways, and other public rights-of-way; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council finds that it is appropriate to consider the effect on
surrounding businesses that a right-of-way closure may have, especially in regards to the
Americans with Disabilities Act and other related considerations; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council desires to set forth and mandate that the above be
taken into consideration prior to a public right-of-way being abandoned; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: The Cabot City Council herein acknowledges that it has sole legal
authority to abandon or otherwise permanently close a city street, public alleyway, and other
public rights-of-way. Said authority may only be exercised through majority vote of the Cabot
City Council.

SECTION 2: Prior to abandoning or otherwise permanently closing a right-of-way, the
Cabot City Council shall consider any effect on surrounding businesses said closure may have,
especially any effect in regards to the Americans with Disabilities Act and other related
considerations.

SECTION 3: This legislation is in regards to right-of-way abandonments and other
permanent closures. Nothing herein effects the City’s authority to temporarily close city streets,
public alleyways, and other public rights-of-way as permitted by law.

SECTION 4: If any provision of this Ordinance is found to be invalid by the decision

of any court of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining sections,

phrases, and provisions of this Ordinance which remain valid and enforceable. As such, the
provisions of this Ordinance are declared to be severable.

perseverance of the health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of Cabot. An emergency is

City Council Meeting Organizational Structure

1. Work Session Meetings

Work Session meetings shall customarily be held on the first Monday of every month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed.
These Work Session meetings are utilized to allow council members and each standing committee
to discuss details of proposed legislation with City staff in a more informal setting. The Work
Session shall be called to order by the Mayor who will then recognize the chair of each committee
in turn to discuss the items on the agenda relevant to that committee. Each committee chair shall
preside over the discussion of agenda items relevant to his or her committee and may conduct
votes amongst his committee members to forward any piece of proposed legislation on to a regular
council meeting or for any other appropriate purpose. No readings or votes for final passage of
legislation shall be conducted during Work Session meetings.

At the conclusion of each Work Session meeting, a Regular Session Council meeting shall
be held. At this meeting any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action
may be taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. This meeting need not be conducted
if there are no items on its agenda for consideration.

2. Regular Session Meeting

Regular Session meetings shall customarily be held on the third Monday of each month at
6:30 p.m. The date and time may be changed in the case of scheduling conflicts or as needed. At
these meetings any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action may be
taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. Pursuant to state law, these meetings shall
be presided over by the Mayor, with each council member having an opportunity to discuss any
item, make any appropriate motion, and vote when appropriate.

Only items on the agenda may be discussed, read, or voted on, unless the agenda is
amended to add that particular item by 2/3 vote of all elected council members. An item not on
the agenda may be discussed, though not voted on, during the community input section of the
meeting.

Pursuant to state law, any motion to suspend the rules, waive readings, approve or attach
an emergency clause, or similar motion must be passed by 2/3 vote of all elected council members

3. Location
The Cabot Justice Center will be the regular meeting place for the Cabot City Council.

The Cabot City Annex, the Veterans Park Event Center, or other appropriate location may also
be used if needed.

Any council member may request to have an item added to a Work Session meeting agenda. A
Work Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

The agenda for the Regular Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Items may be placed on this agenda by the Mayor, by majority vote of the Council, or by majority
vote of the appropriate committee at a Work Session meeting or other committee meeting. An
item placed on an agenda for a Regular Session meeting through committee vote at a Work
Session shall be placed on the agenda for a Regular Session meeting on a subsequent date. As
an exception to the foregoing, such an item shall be placed on the agenda for the Regular Session
meeting on the same date if a motion to that effect is approved by majority vote of the City
Council. A Regular Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to
council members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

In order to be placed on an agenda, a legislative item must be sponsored by either a
council member or the Mayor. Ifa legislative item is forwarded to the Council from one of the
city’s independent commissions it must be sponsored by that independent commission.

Agendas are considered final once forwarded to council members and legislative items
may not be added after that point except upon 2/3 vote of all elected Council members. However,
an item may be added to the agenda after it was sent out but before the start of the meeting upon
joint agreement of the Mayor and the City Council President Pro Tempore.

6. President Pro Tempore

Ed Long, as longest serving member of the Cabot City Council, is hereby named City
Council President Pro Tempore.

7. Mayor and City Council Relationship

In exercising its management responsibilities, the City Council reserves its authority
to approve policy which represents broad statements of its intentions, approves plans and
programs, and delegates authority of administration to the Mayor, except those rights that
are by law conferred upon or reserved to the city council. Pursuant to state law, the City
Council delegates the authority to the Mayor to hire capable personnel within an approved
wage and salary policy, to plan and establish schedules and to train, supervise and terminate
employees. Per A.C.A. § 14-42-110, the City Council reserves the authority to review the
hiring or removal of a department head and may overturn the hiring or removal of a
department head by the Mayor upon two-thirds majority of all elected Council members.

8. Further Responsibilities of the Mayor

The Mayor has the principal responsibility for directing the operations of the city
government and for advising and assisting the City Council in its deliberations. In connection
with the latter responsibility, the City Council requests the Mayor to furnish it with whatever
data, information, and material it may need to properly carry out its functions in an informed
manner.

The Mayor also has the principal responsibility to ensure that the city's administrative
officers and department heads understand and obey all local, state, and federal laws
pertaining to the city's operations, and when a violation of any law is discovered, that
appropriate disclosure is made to the City Council and proper and adequate disciplinary
measures are taken against the responsible employee or employees.

9. Further Responsibilities of the Council

It is the responsibility of City Council members to be engaged and present at meetings in
representing the residents of Cabot. If any member of the City Council is absent for either three
consecutive meetings or four total meetings in a calendar year then a Resolution of Reprimand
shall be considered by the Council. Absences may be excused at a council member’s request and
by joint agreement of the Mayor and the President Pro Tempore of the City Council.

It is the further responsibility of council members to hold themselves to a high ethical and
moral standard in representing the residents of Cabot. Any member who fails to tive up to these
standards or who brings embarrassment or disrepute to the City Council may also be subject to a
Resolution of Reprimand.

10. City Council and Mayor Cooperation

Efficient management of the city can exist only through mutual understanding and
complete cooperation between the City Council and the Mayor. The Mayor's performance
cannot be of the best unless he is given the latitude to exercise independent judgment in
executing policies of the City Council. The City Council acknowledges that obligation and
gives the Mayor the latitude of judgment and discretion, and expects faithful performance in
carrying out the policies of the City Council.

It shall be understood that administrative authority for the management of the city
rests with the Mayor. Members of the City Council should refrain, as individuals, from giving
specific direction or instruction to city personnel pertaining to the discharge of assigned
duties, however, open communication between aldermen and city employees is encouraged.

Personnel; Police and Fire; Community Development; and Military Affairs. In January of each
year, the Nominating Committee shall designate committee assignments for all City Council

committee assignment preferences to the City Attorney’s office, and the City Attorney’s office
shall then forward those preferences to the upcoming members of the Nominating Committee.
Once committee assignments are established by the Nominating Committee, each other
committee shall through majority vote select its own chair from among its own members.

members. Ifa committee is unable to reach a decision through majority vote as to who should
serve as chair of that committee, the issue shall be referred to the full City Council. Upon such
referral, the City Council shall, through majority vote, determine who will serve as chair of that
committee. A committee chair or other committee officer may be removed by majority vote of
that committee.

Any council member may appeal the inclusion or exclusion of a council member on a
standing committee to the full City Council. Any such appeal shall be made in writing to the
office of the City Attorney. The City Attorney’s office shall then coordinate with the Mayor’s
office to ensure that that appeal is included on an upcoming Regular Session meeting agenda.
At such time, the City Council, through majority vote, may either uphold the decision of the
Nominating Committee or change any committee assignments it deems appropriate. The

assigned to the Advertising and Promotion Commission shall serve in that capacity for two-year
terms.

Blake Lively called the meeting to order at 8:33 am
Pledge: Blake Lively

Prayer: Blake Lively

Roll Call: Candy Miller

Funding Request-_Junior Auxiliary of Cabot, Rachael Fratesi — Strawberry Fest (BUDGETED)

Cabot Parks & Rec, Travis Young — Pool Heater (NON-BUDGETED) The request was to fund a new pool heater for

second being made by Stephen Redd. Alli voted and funding was unanimously approved.

Funding Request Recap- Building Bridges, Laura Haywood — Taste and Talent (BUDGETED)

Minutes- The commissioners reviewed the minutes from the December 2024 meeting. A motion to accept the minutes
as written was made by Matt Webber and the second by Greg Jones. The December 2024 minutes were unanimously
accepted as written.

Financial Report - The commissioners reviewed the financials for December 2024. Motion to accept Financials was
made by Stephen Redd and second by Greg Jones. The December 2024 financial report was unanimously accepted as
written.

Chamber Report — None

Cabot Parks & Rec — Travis Young reported that their Noon Year’s Eve was a success with over 700 participants. The
Arkansas Aquatics Conference begins today with Cabot Parks and Rec hosting the event. Winter sports will be ending
in February, and spring sports will begin soon thereafter, with sign ups already under way. The first volleyball
tournament of the year was the past weekend with 92 teams in attendance.

City of Cabot Economic Development- Alicia Payseno reported that they received their Trendsetter City Award last
week. Olive Garden will have its ribbon cutting this Friday and will officially open their doors on Monday. The leases
with Lyons College have been completed. The signing and ceremony for Lyons College will be held February 6" at the
new Justice Center. Buffalo Wild Wings will be building beside Olive Garden.

General discussion— The 2025 budget was brought up for discussion. Greg Jones presented several options to
consider for an increase in revenue for the budget. After much discussion of both the expected revenue and expected
budget funding requests for the upcoming year, it was suggested that the budget revenue be raised 10% over last year
for the 2025 year. A motion was made by Stephen Redd with a second by Greg Jones to accept the 2025 budget as
presented, to include a revenue increase of 10% over last year. All voted and it was unanimously approved.

The State of the City
March 18, 2025
To Members of the City Council and the Citizens of Cabot:

It is with a happy heart that I would like to report that Cabot is in great shape. Overall, the state
of our city is positive and trending upward. The new state of the art Justice Center was just
completed and the police and courts moved all operations in January and Lonoke County’s 911
Communication Center should be moving into the Justice Center during April. This 911
Communication Center will address all emergency calls for the county of Lonoke.

We shall see more restaurants with the opening of a second Taco Bell, a second Starbucks, a
Whataburger, a H tea O restaurant and Buckman Brewhouse. And with the opening of the Cabot
Sportsplex in May of 2024, Cabot hotels, retail centers and restaurants are doing very with the
thousands of people coming to our city each weekend due to our sports tourism efforts. Just last
weekend, we had over 7,000 visitors in our city.

We are in discussions with other large restaurants and retail centers, but the big item for 2025 is
the building of the state’s first veterinary school in Cabot, which will open in August 2026. It
will include Lyon College’s school of veterinary medicine as well as Cabot’s Animal Support
Services complex. A new road will be constructed by the county Judge that will connect this
college to the freeway for easy access by the public.

There are great things to come in 2025. Let’s take a look back at 2024.

Cabot had a very prosperous 2024. We made strides in all areas of the city. During 2024, the
following highlights occurred (this is just some of the highlights, not inclusive of all activity):

Community and Economic Development

We just finished our internet project to provide all homes in Cabot with fiber internet. We are
now the only city in the state of Arkansas that has high speed fiber to each home and the only
city that owns all of their lines. Last week we saw our 2,600th customer added in Cabot to this
internet structure. The system is producing big results in our community with little complaints.
--- page 10 (OCR) ---
Cabot had a tremendous economic growth year with total new business licenses issued of 190.
Among those we had some major new business, such as Aldi, Olive Garden, Hampton Inn,
O'Reilly Auto Parts, Overtime, and Pediatric Plus

We had 105 commercial real estate transactions which totaled $32,152,572.00.

Cabot’s average home price (April 2023) was $239,000 (15.6% increase YoY) with total housing
lots sold from 2020 to 2024 of 701 properties.

Cabot’s economic indicators show steady growth in business development, real estate, and retail
sectors, supported by a strong workforce and increasing population.

Police Department

The Police Department’s accreditation was completed in February of 2024, which makes us one
of the very few in the state to obtain this accreditation out of over 600 cities and towns. We now

have two canines in service and were just one police officer away from being fully staffed at the
end of 2024.

The department was busy with 576 investigations, 100 search warrants served, and 145 felony
drug arrests seizing $278,000 in US currency, 13 pounds of cocaine and 114 pounds of
marijuana. In addition, the department wrote 1011 accident reports, 1,911 incident reports, 111
felony requests, 346 misdemeanor arrests, 160 DWI’s, and 6,234 traffic stops, which resulted in
1,947 traffic citations and 4,237 traffic warnings.

We also had 4,552 new cases filed in District Court in 2024 which is over 1,000 more filings
than 2023.

Fire Department

The Fire Department had an increase in calls in 2024 with a total of 3,234, which 49 were
structure and property fires, saving an estimated $17 million in business and personal property—
more than double the amount in 2023. This success is attributable in part to increased training
and decreased response times achieved through district restructuring in 2024. We have
maintained full staffing levels and added a new Operations and Maintenance Officer.

After several years of planning, we licensed our first firefighters as Advanced EMTs, providing
our city with a more advanced level of emergency care. We will continue this specialized
training in the future. Additionally, the department was able to implement a bike team for special
events like the April Eclipse, Strawberry Fest, and Cabot Fest. And with our new training
facility operational, we will be even more ready in the future to do great things.

Construction Services

Six large construction projects were completed during the year. The projects include the remodel
of Station 4 for the fire department, kitchen remodel for the Peak Center, CASS program office
--- page 11 (OCR) ---
remodel, construction of the CASS Community Gardens, City Hall’s public men and women’s
restrooms, and major repairs to the library.

Senior Services

The Peak Center increased their average attendance to 64 people from 27 people in 2021; and the
average daily meals prepared for consumption each day from 24 people in 2021 to 58 people in
2024. During Thanksgiving we fed an all time high of 127 people. Participation in excursions
also increased and there was good attendance in all activities, which were new average records.

Animal Services

Our euthanasia number in 2024 decreased to 9, from our all time high in 2010 of 406. Even
though 9 was too many, it’s a great feat for our No Kill City. Our cash donation and grants were
$157,600 and our in-kind contributions totaled $171,942.

We also helped our neighboring cities and counties. We had requests and we accommodated
Clarksville, Helena/West Helena, West Memphis, Wynne, Benton, Austin, Searcy, Morrilton,
Russellville, Pine Bluff and Hot Springs.

Street Department

Three new laborers and one new equipment operator was added to keep up with our
beautification and demands of the city’s day to day operations. We purchased a new Kubota 80
Series Excavator to help with our construction of streets and drainage.

We completed drainage projects at Campbell Drive, North St., Sunset Dr, Birchwood Circle,
Southaven Ave, Linda Lane and Rosebud Circle.

We completed 1,520 work orders, 17,171 feet of drainage work, 30,656 sq feet of asphalt repairs,
repaired 159 street lights, and 404 traffic work orders.

We also opened up Elm Street as a new traffic corridor for relief to our downtown Main Street.

Public Works

Permits issued during 2024 was 1,147. Inspections were 2,715 (Inspections range from framing,
footing, RI electrical, HVAC, RI plumbing, roofing, meter loop, re-inspection, yard lines, etc.)

Certificate of Occupancies issued were 155.

Code enforcement cases were 652 (call-in complaints & route observations) Cases range
from condemnations, sanitation of property, high grass, inoperable vehicles, vehicles blocking
sidewalks, gravel driveways, stormwater, etc.

Approximately 2,688 calls received from residents regarding waste collection (missed pick-ups
of trash, recycle, yard waste, limbs, broken carts, etc.).
--- page 12 (OCR) ---
Financial Summary

We have $7,710,523 in cash in the General Fund and $1,802,396 in the Street Fund while
maintaining a budget of $20,103, 835 in 2024. Our legislative audit for the prior year didn’t
have any adjustments and was a clean report, which shows how serious we are with our financial
responsibilities. Our financial statement that will be presented to the public is attached for your
review for 2024.

Overall, as stated above, the City of Cabot is in great shape and 2025 is showing signs of being
another incredible year for the people of Cabot. Thanks to all elected officials, city employees
and caring residents, Cabot continues to make much needed progress, but we are not finished.

Much needed progress has to be done in traffic and we are working hand in hand with ARDOT
and our state legislature. We have also hired a traffic engineer to help with signal relief and
overall gridlock we have been experiencing on a daily basis. The end of 2025 should have the
bidding out of our new overpasses and roundabouts at Exits 16 and 19, that will bring much
needed traffic relief to our central and southern interchanges. In addition, Highway 5 will
become a four-lane highway from Highway 89 to Greystone Community. All in all, hundreds of
millions of dollars have been committed to Cabot and its exciting to see this come to fruition.

Iam honored to serve you as mayor and I will continue to do the things we need to do to make
Cabot a safe place to live. Thank you for your support. It takes all of us working together to
achieve these goals.

AN RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING POLICIES REGARDING THE
CITY’S FIXED ASSET LIST; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the State Law requires cities to maintain a fixed asset list and empowers cities

WHEREAS, the provisions set forth herein are in furtherance of and compliance with
A.C.A. 14-59-107 and other applicable law; and

WHEREAS, the City of Cabot’s policies and practices in regards to its fixed asset list shall
be established as set forth herein.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Consistent with A.C.A. 14-59-107 and other applicable law, the office of
the City Clerk~Treasurer shall maintain, and amend as necessary, the City’s fixed asset list. The
list shall be in compliance with the requirements of A.C.A. 14-59-107 and other applicable law.
For purposes of this list, a “fixed asset” is defined as property owned by the City of Cabot which
has both: an expected useful life of at least one year; and a value or purchase price that is equal to
or greater than $5,000.

that are in conflict with this legislation are to be hereby discontinued and repealed to the extent
of the conflict. Items currently on the fixed asset list that are not in compliance with the policies
set forth herein are to be removed from the list by the office of the City Clerk~Treasurer. This

RESOLUTION NO. 8 OF 2025
A RESOLUTION REGARDING THE HIRING OF ADDITIONAL
CABOT FIRE DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL; AMENDING THE
GENERAL FUND OF THE 2025 ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET;
REGARDING THE MINIMAL STAFFING ON A FIRE APPARATUS;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Due to the forthcoming purchase of an additional aerial apparatus, the
Cabot City Council desires for the City of Cabot to hire additional employees to serve as
firefighters in the Cabot Fire Department; and

WHEREAS, the City Council further desires that said additional employees are to be hired
across 2025 and 2026 as set forth below; and

WHEREAS, the City Council herein amends the General Fund of the 2025 Annual
Operating Budget in furtherance of hiring the additional employees authorized herein

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The City of Cabot is hereby authorized and, to the extent allowed by
law, directed to hire twelve additional firefighters for the Cabot Fire Department as set forth
herein. To the extent that qualified, capable, and acceptable candidates can be found, six of
these firefighters shall be hired by the end of 2025 and the remaining six shall be hired by
the end of 2026. To the extent that the required number of qualified, capable, and
acceptable candidates cannot be found and hired within those timeframes, the City shall

continue its efforts to find and hire such candidates.

SECTION 2: The City Council acknowledges that the potential cost of the new hires
for 2025 is up to $313,009.50, and the potential cost for solely the 2026 new hires is up to
$496,122. The total cost of all twelve employees going forward thereafter will be at least
$878,940 per year. The General Fund of the 2025 Annual Operating Budget is hereby

amended to accommodate the 2025 hires authorized herein.

RESOLUTION NO. 10 OF 2025

A RESOLUTION CONCERNING EMPLOYEE TRAVEL EXPENSES;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, pursuant to state law, the Cabot City Council has wide-ranging authority
over the City’s annual operating budget and appropriations thereof; and

WHEREAS, prior to enactment of this Resolution, it was allowable to use City funds to
pay for employee hotel and lodging accommodations within sixty miles of the employee's
residence, as shown in the attached Exhibit A. The City Council desires to change City policy and.

practice regarding the use of City funds to pay for employee hotel accommodations in certain
situations, as consistent with the provisions set forth herein.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: From the effective date of this Resolution going forward, City funds
may not be used to pay for a hotel or other lodging accommodation for a City employee or
City official unless the training, conference, meeting, or other event in question is at least
sixty miles from the primary residence of the employee or official.

SECTION 2: The City is hereby authorized and directed to update the City of

Cabot Personnel Handbook to include the restrictions imposed herein.

SECTION 3: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its

passage.

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Ed Long, Kyle Pickard, Matt
Webber, and Corey Spangler. Others present were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney
Ben Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy
Yocom also attended.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned to approve the March 4 minutes.
The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Spangler, seconded by Mr. Redd, motioned to approve the March 18 minutes.
The motion passed unanimously.

AMENDED RESOLUTION NO. 10 OF 2025

A RESOLUTION CONCERNING EMPLOYEE TRAVEL EXPENSES;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, pursuant to state law, the Cabot City Council has wide-ranging authority
over the City’s annual operating budget and appropriations thereof; and

WHEREAS, prior to enactment of this Resolution, it was allowable to use City funds to
pay for employee hotel and lodging accommodations within sixty miles of the employee’s
residence, as shown in the attached Exhibit A. The City Council desires to change City policy and

practice regarding the use of City funds to pay for employee hotel accommodations in certain
situations, as consistent with the provisions set forth herein.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: From the effective date of this Resolution going forward, City funds
may not be used to pay for a hotel or other lodging accommodation for a City employee or
City official unless the training, conference, meeting, or other event in question is at least
sixty miles from Cabot City Hall. Notwithstanding the foregoing, City funds may be used to
pay for a hotel or other lodging accommodations if: during the event in question, inclement
weather occurs which is of sufficient severity to cause school cancellations in either Cabot
or the location of the event; or the provision of a hotel or other lodging accommodation
would constitute a reasonable accommodation for a City employee or City official who
requests such an accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act or other similar

law.
SECTION 2: The City is hereby authorized and directed to update the City of
Cabot Personnel Handbook to include the restrictions imposed herein.

SECTION 3: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its

passage.

participate in the U.S. Department of Commerce Financial Assistance Award Grant Program.

Extension Project, was approved to proceed. The grant will provide funds up to $1,900,000,
pursuant to the terms thereof, for the project; and

WHEREAS, Pursuant to said approval and the authorizations given under Resolution 31
of 2022, the City solicited sealed competitive bids for completion of the project in question.
The Cabot City Council herein finds that the City properly engaged in competitive bidding under
all applicable legal provisions and that Mitchell Oilfield Services returned the lowest responsible
bid for the entire project. The City Council recognizes that a lower bid was returned by a
different company, however that bid did not encompass the entire project, as set forth in Exhibit
A, and was therefore properly excluded as the lowest responsible bidder; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council acknowledges and approves that the parts of the
project in question that involve water and sewer infrastructure will be done in conjunction with
the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council therefore authorizes the City to enter into an
agreement with Mitchell Oilfield Services for the completion of the Cabot Utility Infrastructure
Extension Project.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter into
an agreement with Mitchell Oilfield Services for the completion of the Cabot Utility
Infrastructure Extension Project. Said agreement is authorized to be in the amount of
$1,674,997.58 and is to be otherwise generally consistent with the attached Exhibit A,
incorporated herein by this reference. The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are further
authorized to execute any documents or take any other action needed to effectuate the authorized

agreement.

6:30 pm.

This event was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed
here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cwRgFudyYwI&t=215s.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 7:28
pm after the Work Session adjourned. Council Member Stephen Redd led the prayer,
and Council Member Maggie Cope-Waymack led the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Corey Spangler, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Ed Long,
Kyle Pickard, and Matt Webber. Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, Deputy
City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom also attended.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Webber, motioned to approve the minutes of the May
5 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Long, seconded by Mr. Spangler, motioned to approve the minutes of the May
19 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Webber, seconded by Mr. Spangler, motioned to read the legislation by title
only. The motion passed unanimously.

City Council

OLD BUSINESS: ORDINANCE NO. 16 OF 2025 — AN ORDINANCE TO REZONE
PART OF THE NW1/4, NE1/4, SECTION 18M, T-4-N, R-9-W, CITY OF CABOT,
FROM R-2S, MEDIUM DENSITY SINGLE-FAMILY TO I-1 INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT;
AMENDING THE LAND USE PLAN; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by title
only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Long moved, seconded by Mr.
Redd, to adopt the motion. Motion passed with a roll call vote of 8-0. Motion to
adopt the Emergency Clause by Mr. Long, seconded by Mr. Webber, due to the
area needing improvement and needed infrastructure. The motion passed
unanimously.

Mr. Spangler, seconded by Mr. Long, motioned to confirm the new business of items a-
d, Ord. No. 19 - 20; and Res. No. 13 - 14 for this meeting's agenda. The motion passed
unanimously.

RESOLUTION NO. 15 OF 2025
A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING THE RETURN
OF FUNDS TO THE CABOT WATER AND WASTEWATER
COMMISSION UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS; AMENDING THE
GENERAL FUND OF THE 2025 ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET;
AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, in Resolution 8 of 2024, the Cabot City Council authorized the City to
accept the donation of certain specified real property for use as a public park; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council further authorized the City to enter into an agreement
with the Cabot Water and Waste Water Commission to provide sewer infrastructure and related.
services for the proposed park. Pursuant to that agreement the Commission would also contribute
funds towards the infrastructure’s installation. The sewer infrastructure was subsequently installed and
the Commission contributed $50,705.40 to the total cost of the project; and

WHEREAS, as of the passage of this resolution, the real property in question has not been
donated to the City and, as such, has not been dedicated as a public park. The Cabot City Council
therefore determines that the infrastructure installation is not at this time in furtherance of a public

park and that the funds contributed to the project by the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission
to that end should be refunded to it.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: Contingent upon the conditions set forth later in this Section, the
Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized and directed to return the funds paid
by the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission pursuant to the agreement authorized by
Resolution 8 of 2024. The total amount authorized and directed to be paid to the Cabot
Water and Wastewater Commission is $50,705.40. The authorizations and directions
provided for herein shall not take effect if the real property referred to herein and in
Resolution 8 of 2024 has been acquired and by the City and dedicated as a public park by

August 30, 2025.

SECTION 2: The General Fund of the 2025 Annual Operating Budget is hereby

amended to accommodate the $50,705.40 payment authorized and directed herein.

AGAINST REAL PROPERTIES AT VARIOUS LOCATIONS WITHIN THE CITY OF
CABOT FOR FUNDS EXPENDED TO PAY FOR SERVICES RENDERED DUE TO
CODE VIOLATIONS; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot’s Code of Ordinances, the City has
expended funds for services rendered and/or performed by and/or on behalf of the City of Cabot
for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to remove/modify noncompliant
conditions. A list of the relevant real properties is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

WHEREAS, despite notice and demand, the property owners at issue have not paid the
amounts due to the City for services rendered and/or performed as detailed herein; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Arkansas law, tax liens may be created and certified for these
real properties and record property owners as listed in Exhibit A. Furthermore, the lien amounts
should be certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the Lonoke
County Treasurer’s Office or other appropriate county office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: In accordance with the authority granted under A.C.A. 14-54-901 et seq.,
the Cabot City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the City Clerk~Treasurer to certify the
list of real properties and amounts due, plus ten percent, attached hereto to the Lonoke County
Circuit Clerk’s Office, Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office, and any other appropriate office for
inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2025. A list of the relevant
real properties is attached as Exhibit A and is hereby incorporated into this ordinance by this
reference. The real property and corresponding lien amounts listed therein are deemed confirmed
for the purposes of A.C.A. 14-54-903 and other relevant law.

SECTION 2: In accordance with A.C.A 14-54-904, the liens authorized and confirmed
herein by the Cabot City Council may be enforced by the City for ten years. The ten-year period

of time commences upon the filing of the lien with the Lonoke County Circuit Clerk’s office.

Adams Street to the vicinity of South 6" Street. The study includes tributary areas to this

Existing Conditions Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling), and final deliverable includes a report
with recommendations for future capital improvements.

Task 1 - Data Collection and Survey

Task 2 - Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modeling

1) Hydrologic Modeling- Hydrologic analysis will be performed to generate flows and
hydrographs for the 1D/2D Unsteady hydraulic model. City provided drainage areas will be
subdivided to ensure adequate computational points and capture effects of significant
hydrologic features such as culverts, major outfalls, railroad crossings, and other features.
SCS Curve Number methodology will be used for infiltration and runoff parameters. NOAA
Atlas 14 will be used for precipitation estimates for design storms. The hydrologic model will
be executed for a range of storm events including the 5-, 10-, 25-, 50-, and 100-year storms.
Results of the model will be reviewed/compared to existing models, if available.

surface elevations (WSEL) and flooding inundation for the simulated storm events.
Channels and culvert crossings will be modeled in 1D and connected to the 2D surface.

1 INTRODUCTION
The Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission DBA Cabot Waterworks has been vested with the
authority and responsibility for the proper operation, maintenance and improvement of the water and
wastewater systems of the City of Cabot pursuant to the authority provided by Arkansas Code
Annotated §§ 14-234-116, and 14-234-30 I, et seq. The utility is led by Tim Joyner, P.E., with Bruce
Brown as the Financial Manager.

2 WASTEWATER FINANCIAL BACKGROUND
2.1 Current Wastewater Rates
Cabot Waterworks' current Wastewater rates are outlined in Wastewater Rate Ordinance No. 27 of
2008 and Ordinance No. 08 of 2001. Table 2-1 displays the existing Wastewater rate structure for the
Wastewater Department. Unlike some utilities that differentiate rates by customer type, Cabot
Waterworks categorizes its customers into three distinct service areas, each with a unique Service
Flat Charge and unit rate.

All Service Flat Charges include the first 2,000 gallons of consumption, while unit rates are applied
per 1,000 gallons of water usage beyond this threshold. The charges are calculated based on each
customer's recorded water consumption.

2.2 Historic Wastewater Revenue and Expenses
Cabot Waterworks Wastewater Department has provided historic revenue and expenditure records

2.2.1 Revenue
2.2.1.1 Billed Revenue:
Cabot Waterworks generates Wastewater Billed Revenue across all customer connections. This
revenue is derived from a combination of the Service Flat Charge, which includes the first 2,000
gallons of water usage, and the unit rate applied to all recorded water consumption exceeding 2,000
gallons.

2.2.1.2 Non-Rate Revenue:
Cabot Waterworks Wastewater Department collects additional revenue through fees associated
with service connections, disconnections, late charges, and returned checks. The department also

3.2.2 Projecting Annual Unit Billed Revenue
Projecting the annual unit Billed Revenue for the Cabot Waterworks Wastewater Department
requires analyzing consumption patterns. Cabot Waterworks provided water consumption data
grouped into 2,000-gallon intervals, detailing how many connections consumed each interval's
amount monthly. The first interval, 0 to 2,000 gallons, corresponds to the consumption included in
the Service Flat Charge. On average, 21% of all customers consistently consume less than 2,000
gallons per month. Since the average consumption within this group is not provided, a midpoint
assumption of 1,000 gallons per connection is used for those customers.

The following equation represents the Projected Annual Unit Billed Revenue.
 𝑌𝑇𝑈 − (𝐶𝐸𝐵 × 2,000 × 12 + 𝐶𝑆𝐵 × 1,000 × 12)
 𝑃𝐴𝑈𝑅 = × 𝑈𝑅
 1,000
Where,

PAUR = Projected Annual Unit Billed Revenue ($)

YTU = Yearly Total Use (gallons/year)

CEB = Connections that Exceed Service Flat Charge Consumption (79%)

CSB = Connections that Subceed Service Flat Charge Consumption (21%)

UR = Unit Rate ($/1,000 gallons)

In this formula, the number of connections exceeding the minimum consumption (included in the
Service Flat Charge) is multiplied by 2,000 gallons per month and then by 12 months. Similarly, the
number of connections falling short of the minimum consumption is multiplied by the assumed
average of 1,000 gallons per month and then by 12 months. These two values are summed and
subtracted from the total annual billed consumption. By deducting the calculated included
consumption, this formula determines the billable amount of consumption. The resulting difference
is divided by 1,000 to align the units with the unit rate and then multiplied by the unit rate.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 7:41
pm after the Work Session adjourned. Council Member Kyle Pickard led the prayer, and
Council Member Ed Long led the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, Corey Spangler, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Ed Long, Kyle Pickard,
and Matt Webber. James Reid was absent. Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben
Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy
Yocom were present.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Long, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned to approve the minutes of the
August 18 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Spangler, motioned to read the legislation by title only.
The motion passed unanimously.

City Council

RONNY LOE TO THE CABOT PLANNING COMMISSION AND BOARD OF
ADJUSTMENT; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was
read by title only by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Mr. Long motioned to
adopt, seconded by Mr. Webber. Voting in favor were Mr. Long, Mr. Spangler,
Ms. Cope, and Mr. Webber. Voting against were Mr. Redd, Mr. Hillenburg, and
Mr. Pickard, resulting in a 4-3 vote. In accordance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-43-
501(b)(1)(B), Mayor Kincade cast a vote in favor, bringing the final vote count to
5-3, and the motion passed.

WHEREAS, due to violations of the City of Cabot’s Code of Ordinances, the City has

for certain work on real properties located within the city limits to remove/modify noncompliant
conditions. A list of the relevant real properties is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

WHEREAS, despite notice and demand, the property owners at issue have not paid the
amounts due to the City for services rendered and/or performed as detailed herein; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to Arkansas law, tax liens may be created and certified for these
real properties and record property owners as listed in Exhibit A. Furthermore, the lien amounts
should be certified for inclusion in the annual real estate tax statements prepared by the Lonoke
County Treasurer’s Office or other appropriate county office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION 1: In accordance with the authority granted under A.C.A. 14-54-90] et seq.,
the Cabot City Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the City Clerk~Treasurer to certify the
list of real properties and amounts due, plus ten percent, attached hereto to the Lonoke County
Circuit Clerk’s Office, Lonoke County Treasurer’s Office, and any other appropriate office for
inclusion as tax liens on the annual real property tax statements for 2025. A list of the relevant
real properties is attached as Exhibit A and is hereby incorporated into this ordinance by this
reference. The real property and corresponding lien amounts listed therein are deemed confirmed
for the purposes of A.C.A. 14-54-903 and other relevant law.

SECTION 2: In accordance with A.C.A 14-54-904, the liens authorized and confirmed
herein by the Cabot City Council may be enforced by the City for ten years. The ten-year period.

of time commences upon the filing of the lien with the Lonoke County Circuit Clerk’s office.

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council is empowered by state law to adopt legislation
providing for the appointment and terms of Cabot Planning Commission members; and

Planning Commission and the community is better served if all Planning Commission members
reside within city limits; and

WHEREAS, therefore the Cabot City Council herein amends Section 2-208 of the Code
of Cabot to require that all Planning Commission members reside within Cabot city limits; and

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS:

SECTION 1: The Code of Cabot Section 2-208 is hereby amended as set forth in
Exhibit “A”, attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: The membership of any Cabot Planning Commission member living
outside of Cabot City limits upon this Ordinance taking effect shall be vacated. The Mayor shall
make an appropriate nomination to fill any such vacancy, subject to the confirmation of the
Cabot City Council. In accordance with state law, any Planning Commission member whose
membership is vacated by the provisions of this Ordinance shall remain a full Planning
Commission member until his or her replacement is confirmed through majority vote of the
Cabot City Council.

SECTION 3: Any municipal legislation or portion of municipal legislation in conflict
with this Ordinance is hereby repealed to the extent of the conflict.

Locked-off. Any customer whose water service meter has been Disconnected or Locked-off by the
Utility will be assessed a Re-connection fee in addition to any and all past-due amounts, penalties,
and fees. No customer shall be reconnected unless and until all past-due amounts, penalties, and
fees, including the Re-connection fee, have been paid in full.

B. Account Termination. When an account becomes delinquent for 30 days, the
Utility shall mail notice to the location receiving service notifying the customer that the delinquent
account is being terminated. If payment is not received within 10 days, the Utility may terminate

the delinquent account and liquidate the customer’s deposit to offset any and all debts owed to the

monthly billing or late notice processing.

Section 9. Billing Disputes. Billing disputes may be initiated by any customer by contacting
the Utility. Upon receipt of a billing dispute, the Utility shall perform an investigation to compile
relevant facts. Upon completing the investigation, the Utility shall compile a synopsis of the facts,
all findings of its investigation, and all documents submitted by the complainant and forward the
same to the Chairperson of the Commission for a final decision. After considering all relevant
information presented by both the Utility and the complainant, the Chairperson, or the
Chairperson’s designee, shall render a decision regarding the proper amount of the bill.

3.2.2 Projecting Annual Unit Billed Revenue

Projecting the annual unit Billed Revenue for the Cabot Waterworks Wastewater Department
requires analyzing consumption patterns. Cabot Waterworks provided water consumption data
grouped into 2,000-gallon intervals, detailing how many connections consumed each interval's
amount monthly. The first interval, 0 to 2,000 gallons, corresponds to the consumption included in
the Service Flat Charge. On average, 21% of all customers consistently consume less than 2,000
gallons per month. Since the average consumption within this group is not provided, a midpoint
assumption of 1,000 gallons per connection is used for those customers.

The following equation represents the Projected Annual Unit Billed Revenue.

YTU — (CEB x 2,000 x 12+ CSB x 1,000 x 12) UR

Where,

PAUR = Projected Annual Unit Billed Revenue ($)

YTU = Yearly Total Use (gallons/year)

CEB = Connections that Exceed Service Flat Charge Consumption (79%)
CSB = Connections that Subceed Service Flat Charge Consumption (21%)
UR = Unit Rate ($/1,000 gallons)

In this formula, the number of connections exceeding the minimum consumption (included in the
Service Flat Charge) is multiplied by 2,000 gallons per month and then by 12 months. Similarly, the
number of connections falling short of the minimum consumption is multiplied by the assumed
average of 1,000 gallons per month and then by 12 months. These two values are summed and
subtracted from the total annual billed consumption. By deducting the calculated included
consumption, this formula determines the billable amount of consumption. The resulting difference
is divided by 1,000 to align the units with the unit rate and then multiplied by the unit rate.

6:30 pm.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council at 6:30

led the pledge of allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Brandon
Hillenburg, James Reid, Stephen Redd, Maggie Cope, Ed Long, Kyle Pickard, Matt
Webber, and Corey Spangler. Others present were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney
Ben Hooper, Deputy City Attorney Courtnie Holt, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy
Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Mr. Redd, seconded by Mr. Reid, motioned to approve the minutes of the
September 9 meeting. The motion passed unanimously.

Mr. Webber, seconded by Mr. Hillenburg, motioned only to read the legislation by
title. The motion passed unanimously.

City Council

addressed, Mr. Webber moved, seconded by Mr. Spangler, to accept the bid
from Waste Connections. The motion passed unanimously.

3.2.2 Projecting Annual Unit Billed Revenue

Projecting the annual unit Billed Revenue for the Cabot Waterworks Wastewater Department
requires analyzing consumption patterns. Cabot Waterworks provided water consumption data
grouped into 2,000-gallon intervals, detailing how many connections consumed each interval's
amount monthly. The first interval, 0 to 2,000 gallons, corresponds to the consumption included in
the Service Flat Charge. On average, 21% of all customers consistently consume less than 2,000
gallons per month. Since the average consumption within this group is not provided, a midpoint
assumption of 1,000 gallons per connection is used for those customers.

The following equation represents the Projected Annual Unit Billed Revenue.

YTU — (CEB x 2,000 x 12+ CSB x 1,000 x 12) UR

In this formula, the number of connections exceeding the minimum consumption (included in the

number of connections falling short of the minimum consumption is multiplied by the assumed
average of 1,000 gallons per month and then by 12 months. These two values are summed and
subtracted from the total annual billed consumption. By deducting the calculated included
consumption, this formula determines the billable amount of consumption. The resulting difference
is divided by 1,000 to align the units with the unit rate and then multiplied by the unit rate.

1. Purpose

The purpose of this Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is to establish the terms and
conditions under which the Arkansas State Police (“ASP”) will use and operate the property
located at 208 North 1st Street, Cabot, Arkansas 72023 (“Property”), owned by the City of
Cabot (“City”), as a driver’s license testing center.

Il. Responsibilities and Obligations of the ASP

1. Operational Use: The ASP will use the Property primarily for the purpose of conducting
driver’s license testing and local ASP Trooper law enforcement operations. ASP’s use of
the Property under this MOU is limited to the approximately 3200 square feet on the right
side of the building. This includes the area labeled as “council chambers” on the attached
Exhibit A (incorporated herein by this reference) and the adjoining offices and rooms,
including the space labeled as “collections” on Exhibit A. ASP will share use of the
entryway and the restrooms on the right side of the building as shown in Exhibit A with
any other parties that the City authorizes to use the building. ASP will evenly share space
for both interior and exterior signage with any other parties that the City authorizes to use
the building.

2. Compliance with Laws: The ASP agrees to comply with all applicable federal, state, and
local laws and regulations in the operation of the driver’s license testing center and local
law enforcement operations. ASP will have the nature and placement of any exterior
signage pre-approved by the City to ensure compliance with city code.

3. Security and Safety: The ASP shall be responsible for ensuring the security and safety
of the Property during its use, including the implementation of any necessary security
measures.

4. Maintenance of Interior: The ASP shall be responsible for the maintenance and
cleanliness of the interior of the Property as may be utilized by the ASP employees
including workspace, office, kitchenette, and private restroom. ASP must have approval

COMPACTION

General: Begin compaction as soon as placed hot-mix paving will bear roller weight without
excessive displacement. Compact hot-mix paving with hot hand tampers or with vibratory-plate
compactors in areas inaccessible to rollers.

Breakdown Rolling: Complete breakdown or initial rolling immediately after rolling joints and
outside edge. Examine surface immediately after breakdown rolling for indicated crown, grade,
and smoothness. Correct laydown and rolling operations to comply with requirements.

Intermediate Rolling: Begin intermediate rolling immediately after breakdown rolling while hot-
mix asphalt is still hot enough to achieve specified density. Continue rolling until hot-mix
asphalt course has been uniformly compacted to the following density:

1. Average Density, Marshall Test Method: 96 percent of reference laboratory density in
accordance with AASHTO T 245, but not less than 94 percent or greater than 100 percent,

2. Average Density, Rice Test Method: 92 percent of reference maximum theoretical density
in accordance with ASTM D2041/D2041M, but not less than 90 percent or greater than 96
percent.

Finish Rolling: Finish roll paved surfaces to remove roller marks while hot-mix asphalt is still
warm.

Edge Shaping: While surface is being compacted and finished, trim edges of pavement to proper
alignment. Bevel edges while asphalt is still hot; compact thoroughly.

Repairs: Remove paved areas that are defective or contaminated with foreign materials and
replace with fresh, hot-mix asphalt. Compact by rolling to specified density and surface
smoothness.

Protection: After final rolling, do not permit vehicular traffic on pavement until it has cooled and
hardened.
